title: Uncertainty quantification and calibrated confidence
bottleneck: Frontier models express confidence that bears little relation to actual correctness — they are confidently wrong as often as hesitantly right. True calibration requires the model to know what it doesn't know, including out-of-distribution detection, but softmax probabilities and verbalized confidence are both poorly calibrated. There is no reliable I-don't-know signal.
why_it_blocks: In medicine, law, and autonomous decisions, acting on an overconfident wrong answer is the primary failure mode. Without calibration, human reviewers can't tell which outputs need checking. Deployers either over-trust confident errors or waste expert time double-checking everything, including correct outputs.
current_state: Conformal prediction and calibration techniques help on narrow tasks but break down on open-ended generation. Frontier models remain systematically miscalibrated. Verbalized confidence correlates with correctness only weakly, and RLHF can actively degrade calibration.
